items: [main] **Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off the default branch; subagents inherit it. Two `task` calls on the same branch each get their own worktree, or `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/<branch>` between them. A dirty branch with unrelated work: patch out, fresh worktree, apply

[main] **Shape: one PR, independent PRs, or a stack.** Decide before committing. One PR when the change is one concern within about 400 changed lines (`skill://git-conventions` Branching). Independent PRs, each off trunk, when the pieces do not need each other. A stack when later pieces need earlier ones and every layer is reviewable and green on its own: a refactor in its own layer below the behaviour change that needs it, and tests in the same layer as the code they test. One task may span several PRs (`Part of <ID>`); one PR finishes at most one task

[main] **Commits.** Commit as you work, in conventional format per `skill://git-conventions`, bodies per `skill://caveman-commit`. Squash-merge keeps only the PR title and body on trunk, so commits inside a PR are working history: tidy them only where it helps the reviewer, folding a fix into the commit it belongs to. A step of the argument that must survive on trunk is a stack layer, not a commit

[main] **Task finalization.** Before the PR opens, finalize the run's task in the branch per `skill://backlog-conventions`: check only proven acceptance criteria and DoD items (`--check-ac <n>`, `--check-dod <n>`), write `--final-summary`, set `For Review` — `pb-land` sets `Done` at landing — and commit the task file with the work. A PR that does not finish the task leaves it `In Progress` and appends notes. Confirm the milestone: `backlog task edit <ID> -m "v0.N <goal>"` when the task serves an open goal, `-m maintenance` when it serves none (`### Releases and milestones`); every open task has one, and every acceptance criterion that this run proved is checked

[main] **Titles.** Conventional Commits, `type(scope): subject`, with type and format per `skill://git-conventions` (Precedence; for a PR the type follows the task's kind — `## PR titles`), the changed area as the scope, and a short imperative subject naming a real symbol when one carries the change. No trailing period. A breaking change takes `type!`. The title becomes one line of the release notes, so it must still match the diff when the PR merges

[main] **Task link and links.** Every PR carries its task per `skill://backlog-conventions`: `(<ID>)` at the end of the title, so the squash commit on `main` keeps it, and `Closes <ID>` (or `Part of <ID>` when more PRs follow) as the first line of the body. When the task has a milestone, the next line is `Milestone: <name>`. Then link what the change answers or depends on, as repo paths or URLs: the spec or design doc, the `DEFECTS.md` or `IMPROVEMENTS.md` row, the upstream doc or changelog relied on. release-please's `chore(main): release X.Y.Z` release PR is exempt — it is the version bump, not work. No task yet: search first (`task_search` / `backlog search`), then create it per the skill; no `backlog/` yet: init it per the skill's `## Setting up a repo`. Neither MCP nor CLI available: stop the phase

[main] **Identity.** End the body with the identities that made the branch: `agent/scripts/omp-identity-rollup.sh` prints each distinct `Agent-Identity` value in the branch's commits. Once the branch is gone the squash commit on `main` is the only record left, so it has to carry them — a PR spanning an `omp update` has two. No commit in the branch has a trailer (human work, or the machinery landed after those commits): drop the section rather than writing `unknown`

[main] **Body by kind.** Default sections, in order, dropping any with nothing to say: `## Why` (intent and approach, no SHAs, no genealogy), `## Scope` (real symbols and paths as bullets, both sides of a rename, no file-by-file essay), `## Tradeoffs` (only rejected alternatives a reviewer would ask about), `## Blast Radius` (one to three sentences: consumers, callers and artifacts touched), `## Verification`. What `## Verification` must show depends on the task's kind: `feature` — the new behaviour exercised on the real surface; `bugfix` — the reproduction failing on trunk and passing on the branch, the same command both times; `refactor` — the same tests or output before and after, and no behaviour change in the diff; `migration` — a dry run on a copy, row or object counts before → after, and the rollback path; `chore` — for a dependency, its changelog link and the run showing nothing else moved, for config the value read back from the running system; `docs`, `spec`, `design`, `investigation`, `content` — the rendered result and its citations checked; `continuous-improvement` — the ledger row it answers and the check that goes red without it; a revert (`revert:` title) — the PR it reverts, why, and the run showing prior behaviour is back. For a performance change, one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form

[main] **Verification a reviewer can rerun.** Each line of `## Verification` names the exact command (or the surface and its steps), its observed outcome, and where to see it: a CI run URL, an artifact path or link, a screenshot. Say plainly what was not run and why. "Tests pass" or "it compiles" without the command is not verification. A PR landed on the self-verified exception (`pb-land`) carries the line `Verdict: self-verified — <reason>` here

[main] **Descriptions.** The PR title and body become the squash commit on trunk once the repo's merge settings are set (`skill://git-conventions` `### GitHub merge settings`), so write for a future reader of `git log`: a briefing, not the diff's lab notebook. Never use `## Summary` or `## Test plan` boilerplate, and keep a commit body from restating its subject. Apply `skill://unslop`. Before commit, reread the diff and cut slop: a comment survives only for a non-obvious why

[main] **PRs.** Open every PR ready, never as a draft, and run `gh pr view <N>` before you refer to PR status. One PR or independent PRs: `gh pr create --base <trunk>` without `--draft`, then `gh pr ready <N>` if it still opens as a draft

[main] **Stacks with `gh stack`.** Build a stack as a GitHub native stack (`gh extension install github/gh-stack`): `gh stack init --base <trunk> <branch-1> [<branch-2> …]` and `gh stack add <branch>` for each later layer, every branch named per `skill://git-conventions` — the command guard refuses a stack command that names no branch, because `gh stack add -m` would generate a date-slug name. `gh stack submit --open` pushes the branches and opens the PRs ready and linked as one stack; then set each PR's title and body with `gh pr edit <N> --title … --body-file …`. Absorb trunk or a changed lower layer with `gh stack sync` or `gh stack rebase`, never by retargeting bases by hand. GitHub checks every layer against the trunk's branch protection and CI
[main] **Readiness.** Confirm each PR is non-draft, carries its task link, and its `## Verification` names runs a reviewer can repeat

[main] **Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building; finish the phase or stack first. Run `pb-babysit` only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists. Push back when feedback drifts from intent. A subagent that opens a PR runs `skill://cross-domain-blindspot-audit`, cuts slop, and returns the URL without babysitting
